article.title: Six-month follow-up of the 'Mi Mejor Plan' school-based prevention program: a pilot cluster randomized controlled trial among early adolescents in Chile.
article.authors: Gaete J, Ríos N, Ramírez S
article.abstract: School-based preventive interventions for adolescent substance use often show limited short-term behavioral effects, with evidence suggesting that sustained impacts may depend on continued exposure and reinforcement strategies such as booster sessions. However, few studies have examined the longitudinal effects of booster implementation on substance use and related psychosocial outcomes in culturally adapted interventions.
